card.title: No classes for students
lines: Friday, December 18 is a teacher planning day. There are no classes for students.
Thursday, December 17 is the last day of classes before the winter break.
The winter break runs from Monday, December 21 to Friday, January 1.
Classes start again on Monday, January 4.
lines_es: El viernes 18 de diciembre es un día de planificación para los maestros. No hay clases para estudiantes.
El jueves 17 de diciembre es el último día de clases antes de las vacaciones de invierno.
Las vacaciones de invierno van del lunes 21 de diciembre al viernes 1 de enero.
Las clases vuelven a empezar el lunes 4 de enero.

decide.title: Decision and reflection
body: Write today's daily entry: Did, Changed, Next.
Add one decision you made today, with its reason.

r-studio.title: Your research work
body: Use your existing feedback.
Choose your most important next step.
Revise, retain or investigate; explain why.
Save your decision and next step; keep prior work.
Individual help is by agreed appointment.
No surveys, interviews or data from other people until Mr. Portela tells you your study is approved.

steps: Choose your most important next step
Save your decision and next step

body_es: Usa la retroalimentación que ya tienes.
Elige tu próximo paso más importante.
Revisa, conserva o investiga; explica por qué.
Guarda tu decisión y tu próximo paso; conserva el trabajo anterior.
La ayuda individual es con cita acordada.
No hagas encuestas ni entrevistas, ni reúnas datos de otras personas, hasta que el Sr. Portela te diga que tu estudio está aprobado.

s-gnote.title: Guest note
body: Ready one page for a single accurate note.
Note how the speaker connects evidence to a claim.
You do not need to cite the talk.

d-7.title: T2: Build one connected argument
body: Order the claims and evidence.
Explain how each supports the conclusion.
Make the meaningful limit visible.
d-7.origin: AP Seminar deck, Revise, share and build the argument (December 7-11), slide 7

d-8.title: T2: Evidence on screen, reasoning aloud
body: Choose a useful visual.
Preserve its source, labels and scale.
Prepare to explain choices and respond to feedback.
d-8.origin: AP Seminar deck, Revise, share and build the argument (December 7-11), slide 8

d-9.title: T2: Sequence the argument
body: State the provisional conclusion.
Locate evidence for each claim.
Include the alternative or limitation.
d-9.origin: AP Seminar deck, Revise, share and build the argument (December 7-11), slide 9

d-10.title: T2: Check the visual evidence
body: Keep only what the listener needs.
Check the original source.
Preserve sound work in the existing deck.
d-10.origin: AP Seminar deck, Revise, share and build the argument (December 7-11), slide 10

d-11.title: T2: Make the transitions meaningful
body: Explain why one point follows another.
Keep speaking responsibilities clear.
Understand research beyond your own section.
d-11.origin: AP Seminar deck, Revise, share and build the argument (December 7-11), slide 11

d-12.title: T2: Show the readiness evidence
body: Explain the central argument and a supported connection.
Name the alternative and limitation.
Identify any essential unfinished work.
d-12.origin: AP Seminar deck, Revise, share and build the argument (December 7-11), slide 12

e-3.title: Paired rehearsal
body: Present, respond, listen and record.
Each team presents once.
Choose the change the evidence warrants.
e-3.origin: AP Seminar deck, Rehearse, explain and repair (December 14-17), slide 3

e-5.title: Make and check one consequential repair
body: Locate the feedback and original passage.
Change the explanation or evidence connection.
Rehearse the change and explain why it helps.
e-5.origin: AP Seminar deck, Rehearse, explain and repair (December 14-17), slide 5

body: Save the report and explained revision.

body: Read the complete passage and all three prompts.
Analyze the author's argument and evidence.
Work independently in the agreed response location.

Or have a second listener restate the repaired reasoning.

Write your introduction and one body paragraph.
Work on your own: 40 minutes, timed and typed.

lines: Revise one part your feedback names: introduction, literature review or method.

Debajo, escribe qué cambiaste y por qué.

lines: Begin from one named next step in your existing feedback.
If you are blocked, write the exact question.
Individual help is by agreed appointment.
Work from your feedback and your last daily entry.
Also write what evidence would change today's decision.
State the provisional conclusion.
Locate evidence for each claim.
Include the alternative or limitation.
Mark a claim the evidence does not yet support as a gap.
Read your finding from a prepared note, and a teammate restates it.
Locate the evidence for your own claim.
State the strongest fair case for the alternative your team did not choose.
Explain why your conclusion still holds, or how it changes.
Locate the feedback and original passage.
Change the explanation or evidence connection.
Rehearse the change and explain why it helps.
Leave a short note beside the change: what changed, why, and what still needs work.
Point to the exact slide or outline passage.
Say what the listener could not follow.
Keep the old version visible while you change it.
If the evidence does not support the claim, qualify the claim or name the gap.
Have a listener restate the reasoning after the change.
When your team is called, give the central argument and the evidence that connects it.
Each member answers a question about an actual decision by pointing to the work.
While you wait, work on your existing practice priority at your table.
You may hold your speaking outline while you present.
Point to the exact slide, source or note behind your answer.
While you wait, finish one part of your practice priority.
Be ready for a follow-up question about a limit of your team's conclusion.
While you wait, check that every claim in your outline points to its evidence.

pb.en: My introduction and paragraph follow one clear line of reasoning.
pb.es: Mi introducción y mi párrafo siguen una línea de razonamiento clara.

pb.es: Uso y explico evidencia de al menos dos fuentes.

pb.es: Relaciono las perspectivas de las fuentes que uso.

claim.def_en: What the author says is true.
claim.def_es: Lo que el autor dice que es cierto.

limit.def_es: Lo que la evidencia no puede mostrar.

attribution.def_en: Saying which source an idea comes from.
attribution.def_es: Decir de qué fuente viene una idea.

synthesis.def_en: Connecting sources to explain something new.
synthesis.def_es: Conectar fuentes para explicar algo nuevo.

perspective.def_en: A point of view on an issue.
perspective.def_es: Un punto de vista sobre un tema.

record.def_en: One documented observation or entry in your data.
record.def_es: Una observación o entrada documentada en tus datos.

method.def_en: How you will collect and analyze evidence.
method.def_es: Cómo vas a recolectar y analizar la evidencia.

feedback.def_en: Comments on your work that guide revision.
feedback.def_es: Comentarios sobre tu trabajo que guían la revisión.

revision.def_en: A change to your work, with a reason.
revision.def_es: Un cambio en tu trabajo, con una razón.

reverse-outline.def_en: A note beside each paragraph of your draft that says what the paragraph does.
reverse-outline.def_es: Una nota junto a cada párrafo de tu borrador que dice lo que hace ese párrafo.

alternative.def_en: Another reasonable conclusion or solution that the same evidence could support.
alternative.def_es: Otra conclusión o solución razonable que la misma evidencia podría apoyar.

provisional.def_en: Held for now, and open to change if new evidence appears.
provisional.def_es: Válido por ahora, y abierto a cambiar si aparece nueva evidencia.

transition.def_en: The words that explain why one point follows another.
transition.def_es: Las palabras que explican por qué un punto sigue a otro.

line-of-reasoning.def_en: The order of claims an author uses to lead to a conclusion.
line-of-reasoning.def_es: El orden de las afirmaciones que un autor usa para llegar a una conclusión.

literature-review.def_en: The part of your paper that shows what is already known, how the sources relate, and the gap your study addresses.
literature-review.def_es: La parte de tu trabajo que muestra lo que ya se sabe, cómo se relacionan las fuentes y el vacío que tu estudio atiende.

target.why_en: Practice for Part B of the AP Seminar end-of-course exam, and for the Team Multimedia Presentation (TMP), Performance Task 1.
target.why_es: Práctica para la Parte B del examen de fin de curso de AP Seminar y para la Presentación Multimedia en Equipo (TMP), Tarea de Desempeño 1.

lines: Have your device ready for the timed Part B planning task.

lines: What is your next step after today's Part B task and rehearsal? Write it in your current work.
Save your work in its existing location.
lines_es: ¿Cuál es tu próximo paso después de la tarea de la Parte B y el ensayo de hoy? Escríbelo en tu trabajo actual.
Guarda tu trabajo donde ya está.

next.en: After the winter break, on Tuesday, January 5: short teacher practice presentations begin. Your practice evidence stays together until then.
next.es: Después de las vacaciones de invierno, el martes 5 de enero: empiezan las presentaciones de práctica breves con el profesor. Tu evidencia de práctica queda junta hasta entonces.

target.en: I can present my team's argument and evidence in a short practice presentation and explain a real decision we made.
target.es: Puedo presentar el argumento y la evidencia de mi equipo en una presentación de práctica breve y explicar una decisión real que tomamos.
target.why_en: Feeds the Team Multimedia Presentation (TMP), AP Seminar Performance Task 1: an argument a listener can follow, and answers about the team's real choices.
target.why_es: Prepara la Presentación Multimedia en Equipo (TMP), Tarea de Desempeño 1 de AP Seminar: un argumento que quien escucha puede seguir, y respuestas sobre las decisiones reales del equipo.

lines: Open your team's current outline or deck and your evidence.
Find the evidence for each claim and one decision you can explain.
lines_es: Abre el esquema o la presentación actual de tu equipo y tu evidencia.
Busca la evidencia de cada afirmación y una decisión que puedas explicar.
